evidence: Agent-visible public surface = task/instruction.md plus everything the env Dockerfile copies (instructions/ -> /instructions, assets/ -> /assets; Dockerfile lines 14-15). Frozen bytes match manifest: instruction.md c8743c57..., hireops_rules.md dc739547..., integration.md 1b56dd3f..., seed_data.json 22df2a00..., Dockerfile 0a75419e.... (1) Skill-reference grep `judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel|probe|gate|grad|verif|oracle|harness|polish|visual|functional|test` (case-insensitive) over instruction.md and both /instructions notes returns a single hit, hireops_rules.md:172 'at the latest on the next', a false substring match on 'latest'. The same grep over seed_data.json returns nothing. (2) Probe/sentinel literals: an uppercase-token scan of all tests/ prompts, judge.toml files, app_context.md and test.sh finds only harness variable names (APP_COPY, APP_DB, APP_ENTRY, APP_RESTART_HELPER, REWARDKIT_JUDGE/MODEL, ZERO_REWARD_JSON, LOG_DIR, EXERCISED). None appears in the brief, the notes or the seed. DB_PATH, NODE_PATH and PORT are public runtime-contract variables, not sentinels. (3) Verbatim overlap: 12-word shingles show no overlap between the public files and any tests/ file. 7-word shingles find only five runs of 7-8 words, all in tests/scored/functional (for example 'the card was changed and by whom', 'its most recent 30 messages oldest of'). In every case a criterion restates a public requirement (direction criterion <- brief). No criterion id, criterion text block, dimension name or weight is exposed. (4) The brief never names the judge, model, rubric, dimensions (functional/polish/visual/gates), weights, /tests paths, score.py, Playwright or the restart tool. Brief line 5 ('within fifteen seconds') and rules section 5 ('within 15 seconds') are product requirements, not grader timing. (5) Borderline item considered and accepted: hireops_rules.md section 8 (lines 197-201) says the runtime 'may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory ... may launch a writable copy of the submitted application' and lists the launch env vars. This states the runtime contract (it matches the test.sh APP_COPY behaviour) so a correct app is not penalised for a cwd assumption. It does not name the grader, its paths, its criteria or a sentinel, and the skill and workbook row 4 expect the runtime contract to be stated. Counterexample attempts: no wording in the public files lets a weak app target a probe value or criterion id, because none is published. A conforming app cannot be disadvantaged by this row. Scope: this is a source review only. No runtime evidence is needed for this row, and none was claimed.
